    Additive subcategories and indecomposable support #

    The adapter needed by the paper: a full, replete subcategory of finitely generated modules which is closed under finite direct sums and direct summands is completely determined by its indecomposable support.

    No Krull--Schmidt multiplicity-uniqueness theorem is used. The only uniqueness input is the existing radical argument IndecomposableSkeleton.not_splitMono_of_labels_ne.

    source
    structure MBDVendor.QSE.IndecomposableSkeleton.AdditiveRepleteSummandSubcategory {R : Type u} [Ring R] :
    Type (max u (w + 1))

    A literal full additive, replete, summand-closed subcategory, represented by its object predicate. Fullness is supplied by carrier.FullSubcategory; finite-biproduct closure includes the empty biproduct, and retract closure implies repleteness.

    • carrier : CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty (FGModuleCat R)
    • biproduct_mem (J : FintypeCat) (F : J.obj → FGModuleCat R) : (∀ (j : J.obj), self.carrier (F j)) → self.carrier (⨁ F)
    • retract_mem {X Y : FGModuleCat R} : ∀ (a : CategoryTheory.Retract X Y), self.carrier Y → self.carrier X

          i ∈ S

          If an indecomposable representative is a retract of an object in add S, its index already lies in S.

          This is the precise substitute for a global Krull--Schmidt uniqueness API: otherwise the split embedding into the displayed sum would have all its components in the endomorphism radical.
